'''Edward Joseph Hoffman''' (January 1, 1942 – July 1, 2004) helped invent the first human [[Positron emission tomography|PET scanner]], a commonly used [[Full-body scan|whole-body scanning]] procedure for detecting diseases like [[cancer]].  Hoffman, with [[Michel Ter-Pogossian]] and [[Michael E. Phelps]], developed the [[Positron Emission Tomography]] scanner in 1973.

Hoffman was born in St. Louis, Missouri. He earned a BS chemistry from [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]] in 1963, his Ph.D. in Nuclear Chemistry from [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in 1970. In 1972 he joined the faculty of [[Washington University School of Medicine]], where he and Michael Phelps began developing what later became known as the PET scanner, used to detect cancer, heart disease and other serious illnesses. In 1975, Phelps and Hoffman moved to the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref>"[http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/senate/inmemoriam/edwardjhoffman.htm IN MEMORIAM] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090505063809/http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/senate/inmemoriam/edwardjhoffman.htm |date=2009-05-05 }} Edward J. Hoffman, Professor of Molecular and Medical Pharmacology, Los Angeles, 1942—2004", Univ of California webpage, accessed online 21 Aug 2008</ref>

Starting in 1976, Hoffman was a professor at [[David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA]] in the Departments of Molecular and Medical Pharmacology and Radiological Sciences.<ref>SR Cherry, [http://www.ieee.org/organizations/pubs/newsletters/npss/0904/remembrance.html "Edward J. Hoffman, Ph.D. A personal reminiscence and remembrance"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080830020912/http://www.ieee.org/organizations/pubs/newsletters/npss/0904/remembrance.html |date=2008-08-30 }}, Edited from remarks made at the memorial service in Los Angeles, July 10, 2004.</ref> In 1999, he authored a book that reviews the biochemical basis of alternative medical treatments for cancer.<ref>Hoffman EJ (1999) [https://books.google.com/books?id=WiIVBWKJhYwC&pg=PA1969 Cancer and the Search for Selective Biochemical Inhibitors] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216000549/https://books.google.com/books?id=WiIVBWKJhYwC&pg=PA1969 |date=2019-12-16 }}, 1st edition, ''CRC Press'', ISBN</ref><ref>Hoffer A, [http://orthomolecular.org/library/jom/2000/articles/2000-v15n04-p224.shtml Book Reviews] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705034641/http://orthomolecular.org/library/jom/2000/articles/2000-v15n04-p224.shtml |date=2008-07-05 }}, ''J Ortho Med'', p.224, Vol. 15, no. 4, 2000</ref> He served as Editor-in-Chief of the journal ''[[IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science]]''.<ref>{{cite news |last=Pearce |first=J |title=Edward J. Hoffman, Medical Imaging Researcher, Dies at 62 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 25, 2004 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/07/25/us/edward-j-hoffman-medical-imaging-researcher-dies-at-62.html}}</ref>

He died of liver cancer in [[Los Angeles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archives |first=L. A. Times |date=August 4, 2004 |title=Edward J. Hoffman, 62; Professor, Co-Inventor of PET Scan Device |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-aug-04-me-passings4.2-story.html |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref>
